the structure of the intracellular region of the amyloid β precursor protein (APP), in complex with the phosphotyrosine binding (PTB)2 domain of Fe65, shows how phosphorylation of APP regulates the interaction between APP and Fe65.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AICD–Fe65 complex is a molecular switch that is regulated by phosphorylation of T668 and by binding to other partners.
the Fe65‐AICD interaction is essential for Aβ generation and that the phosphorylation‐dependent regulation of this interaction may play a role in Aβ regulation.
this work provides the first structural and mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of AICD‐Fe65 complex assembly, and the molecular mechanism of the T668 phosphorylation switch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the structure of the Aβ‐producing APP in complex with the Fe65‐PTP2 domain, which has been shown to be essential for Aβ production.

Fe65‐PTBs bind to AICD in an NPXY motif‐dependent manner, but the binding is regulated by T668 phosphorylation, and the binding of Fe65‐PTPs to AICD can be modulated by AICD‐binding to other proteins.
the AICD–Fe65 complex is regulated by the phosphorylation state of T668, and this regulation is likely to have a significant influence on the processing and trafficking of APP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the Aβ/AICD‐Fe65 complex provides a framework for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for Alzheimer disease.
the AICD‐Fe65 complex structure is the first step toward the elucidation of the molecular basis of AICD‐mediated Alzheimer disease pathogenesis and APP processing regulation.
the structure and the mechanism of the Fe65‐AICD interaction are more complex than anticipated, and may be more relevant to Alzheimer disease than previously thought.
